statement: A square garden has sides of 5 m. Fence posts stand all the way round it: one at every corner and one every 1 m along each side. How many posts are there?

choices.misconception: I counted only the posts between the corners and left out the corner posts.
I added one extra post to finish, as you would on a straight fence.
I counted 6 posts on each side, so every corner post was counted twice.
I counted the 1 m squares that fill the garden instead of the posts round it.

hints: How far is it all the way round?
Walk once round the garden. Every 1 m you reach a new post, and when you get back to the start you are at the first post again, so it is not a new one.
The distance round is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 m, and there is one post for each metre you walk.

solutions.reliable: The distance all the way round is 4 x 5 = 20 m. Walking round, there is a post at every metre mark, and the last metre brings you back to the first post. So there are 20 posts. The idea to keep: on a closed loop, the number of posts equals the number of gaps.
solutions.elegant: Each side has its 5 posts if you count the corner where it starts but not the corner where it ends. 4 sides give 4 x 5 = 20 posts, with every corner counted exactly once. The idea to keep: give each shared corner to just one side.

whyOnTest: It joins perimeter with the fence-post idea, and the closed loop is what makes the usual plus-one wrong.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
